topline.text: A quiet day - no major new policy, inspection or funding story broke nationally or locally in the last 24-48 hours.

The clearest update: Ofsted has confirmed it is extending the pause on routine inspections of National Professional Qualification (NPQ) and early career teacher programme (ECTP) providers through the rest of 2026/27, with normal inspections not resuming until 2027/28.
topline.action: Useful if any staff ask why their NPQ or ECT provider hasn't had a routine Ofsted visit this year.

sections.heading: National: Ofsted extends pause on NPQ and early-career-teacher inspections

items.lede: Ofsted has confirmed a further pause on routine inspections of providers running National Professional Qualifications, now extended to also cover early career teacher programme providers.
items.body: The pause - requested by the Minister for School Standards - runs through the rest of the 2026/27 academic year. Ofsted says it needs the time to bring NPQ and ECTP inspection into line with its current inspection approach, including a new toolkit, operating guide and report card, with sector engagement to follow. Routine inspections are expected to resume in 2027/28.
items.action: Worth a line to CPD leads and anyone currently on an NPQ or supporting an ECT, so they know the lack of a provider inspection this year is expected, not a gap.

box.label: Jargon-buster - NPQ & ECTP
box.intro: Both paused from routine Ofsted inspection this year:
box.text: NPQ (National Professional Qualification) - DfE-funded leadership and specialist qualifications for teachers and leaders. ECTP (Early Career Teacher Programme) - the structured two-year induction support for newly qualified teachers, formerly the ECF.
